scenes.tts: How can fertilizer on land leave deep Bay animals without enough oxygen? Watch one Chesapeake Bay cross-section. The answer begins far from the deep water. The surface may look lively while animals below face a hidden shortage.
scenes.caption: How can fertilizer on land leave deep Bay animals without enough oxygen? Watch one Chesapeake Bay cross-section. The answer begins far from the deep water. The surface may look lively while animals below face a hidden shortage.
scenes.visual: Fill the frame with one Chesapeake Bay cross-section: rainy field and river at left, sunlit surface above, deep channel below. A crab and fish drift near the bottom. COLOR MAP: nutrients gold, algae and plants green, oxygen blue, decomposers gray, animals white. Mark the whole picture 'schematic'. Gold fertilizer grains tremble on the field while blue oxygen dots drift below.
scenes.narration: How can fertilizer on land leave deep Bay animals without enough oxygen? Watch one Chesapeake Bay cross-section. The answer begins far from the deep water. The surface may look lively while animals below face a hidden shortage.

scenes.visual: Keep the moving Bay world visible. Briefly place the title 'Extra Nutrients, Less Deep Oxygen' over the sky, then slide it away. Water and oxygen dots keep moving.

scenes.tts: Rain carries some fertilizer into a creek, then a river. Fertilizer and manure contain nutrients that living things need.
scenes.caption: Rain carries some fertilizer into a creek, then a river. Fertilizer and manure contain nutrients that living things need.
scenes.visual: Rain streaks push gold nutrient particles from the field into the creek. The creek widens into the Bay without a cut. Gold particles keep moving with the current.
scenes.narration: Rain carries some fertilizer into a creek, then a river. Fertilizer and manure contain nutrients that living things need.

scenes.tts: Wastewater and some air pollution add nutrients too. Nutrients help growth, but their effect depends on where they go and how much arrives.
scenes.caption: Wastewater and some air pollution add nutrients too. Nutrients help growth, but their effect depends on where they go and how much arrives.
scenes.visual: Small labeled gold streams from wastewater and air join the river flow. Keep the Bay world continuous and never show more than six labels.
scenes.narration: Wastewater and some air pollution add nutrients too. Nutrients help growth, but their effect depends on where they go and how much arrives.

scenes.tts: Pond water on a sunny windowsill can turn green as algae grow. In the Bay, extra nitrogen and phosphorus can feed fast growth.
scenes.caption: Pond water on a sunny windowsill can turn green as algae grow. In the Bay, extra nitrogen and phosphorus can feed fast growth.
scenes.visual: A tiny window-and-jar inset briefly greens, then transforms into the Bay surface. Green algae dots begin multiplying across the sunlit layer as gold particles arrive.
scenes.narration: Pond water on a sunny windowsill can turn green as algae grow. In the Bay, extra nitrogen and phosphorus can feed fast growth.

scenes.tts: A thick growth is an algae bloom. More nutrients can support more algae, though conditions still matter. The green water can block sunlight from grasses below.
scenes.caption: A thick growth is an algae bloom. More nutrients can support more algae, though conditions still matter. The green water can block sunlight from grasses below.
scenes.visual: Green algae dots thicken into one moving surface patch. A short 'algae bloom' label grows with it, and its shadow reaches the grasses below.
scenes.narration: A thick growth is an algae bloom. More nutrients can support more algae, though conditions still matter. The green water can block sunlight from grasses below.

scenes.tts: Later, algae die and sink. The sinking material carries the next part of the story downward. Now predict: where will oxygen run low, near the surface or in deep water?
scenes.caption: Later, algae die and sink. The sinking material carries the next part of the story downward. Now predict: where will oxygen run low, near the surface or in deep water?
scenes.visual: Some green algae turn gray and fall toward the channel. Put the two choices beside the same cross-section, with blue oxygen dots in both layers.
scenes.narration: Later, algae die and sink. The sinking material carries the next part of the story downward. Now predict: where will oxygen run low, near the surface or in deep water?

scenes.visual: Hold the question over the same moving cross-section. Gray algae continue sinking slowly. Blue oxygen dots drift in both layers, but none vanish yet.

scenes.tts: Deep water runs low on oxygen. Bacteria gather on the dead algae. These decomposers break down dead matter and use dissolved oxygen while they work. The algae are food for decomposers, not direct oxygen thieves.
scenes.caption: Deep water runs low on oxygen. Bacteria gather on the dead algae. These decomposers break down dead matter and use dissolved oxygen while they work. The algae are food for decomposers, not direct oxygen thieves.
scenes.visual: Gray decomposer shapes cluster around settled algae. Each working pulse removes one nearby blue oxygen dot from the deep layer. Surface oxygen keeps drifting and stays plentiful. Label bacteria 'decomposers' only after they gather.
scenes.narration: Deep water runs low on oxygen. Bacteria gather on the dead algae. These decomposers break down dead matter and use dissolved oxygen while they work. The algae are food for decomposers, not direct oxygen thieves.

scenes.tts: Change one ecosystem part, and effects can spread through the system. Here, nutrients change algae, decomposition, oxygen, and animal habitat. Each step changes the conditions faced by the next living part.
scenes.caption: Change one ecosystem part, and effects can spread through the system. Here, nutrients change algae, decomposition, oxygen, and animal habitat. Each step changes the conditions faced by the next living part.
scenes.visual: Without leaving the Bay, briefly highlight the carried path in order: gold nutrients, green algae, gray decomposers, blue oxygen, white animals. A thin pulse travels through the connected shapes; no separate list appears.
scenes.narration: Change one ecosystem part, and effects can spread through the system. Here, nutrients change algae, decomposition, oxygen, and animal habitat. Each step changes the conditions faced by the next living part.

scenes.tts: Summer makes the deep loss harder to replace. Fresher river water floats above saltier Bay water. The layers mix poorly. Warm water also holds less oxygen. Algae fed by spring nutrients can keep sinking and decaying into summer.
scenes.caption: Summer makes the deep loss harder to replace. Fresher river water floats above saltier Bay water. The layers mix poorly. Warm water also holds less oxygen. Algae fed by spring nutrients can keep sinking and decaying into summer.
scenes.visual: Make the upper layer pale blue and the lower layer dark blue. A soft boundary bends but does not break. Surface oxygen dots bounce at the boundary while the deep oxygen field thins. A sun warms the surface with slow waves.
scenes.narration: Summer makes the deep loss harder to replace. Fresher river water floats above saltier Bay water. The layers mix poorly. Warm water also holds less oxygen. Algae fed by spring nutrients can keep sinking and decaying into summer.

scenes.tts: Fish and crabs often move away from low oxygen. Adult oysters are fixed in place. Animals that cannot leave may become sick or die. Bacteria still live there. Low oxygen shrinks the deep habitat available to many animals.
scenes.caption: Fish and crabs often move away from low oxygen. Adult oysters are fixed in place. Animals that cannot leave may become sick or die. Bacteria still live there. Low oxygen shrinks the deep habitat available to many animals.
scenes.visual: The fish swims upslope and the crab walks toward shallower water. An oyster remains attached at the bottom while its motion slows. Decomposer shapes continue pulsing, so the deep zone never looks empty.
scenes.narration: Fish and crabs often move away from low oxygen. Adult oysters are fixed in place. Animals that cannot leave may become sick or die. Bacteria still live there. Low oxygen shrinks the deep habitat available to many animals.

scenes.tts: This process is eutrophication: extra nutrients feed too much algae growth, which can lead to low oxygen. Fertilizer does not take oxygen itself.
scenes.caption: This process is eutrophication: extra nutrients feed too much algae growth, which can lead to low oxygen. Fertilizer does not take oxygen itself.
scenes.visual: Reverse-trace the same world from the deep low-oxygen patch back to decomposers, sinking algae, bloom, river, and field. Bracket the moving path with 'eutrophication' and 'can lead to low oxygen'.
scenes.narration: This process is eutrophication: extra nutrients feed too much algae growth, which can lead to low oxygen. Fertilizer does not take oxygen itself.

scenes.tts: The effects travel through living connections. The word names the nutrient-driven process, not every patch of green water.
scenes.caption: The effects travel through living connections. The word names the nutrient-driven process, not every patch of green water.
scenes.visual: Let one pulse travel through the gold-to-green-to-gray-to-blue path. Then dim an unrelated green patch outside the bracket so the label does not overreach.
scenes.narration: The effects travel through living connections. The word names the nutrient-driven process, not every patch of green water.

scenes.tts: A useful model follows the change from its starting point to each connected part. It also asks what could weaken, strengthen, or interrupt the path.
scenes.caption: A useful model follows the change from its starting point to each connected part. It also asks what could weaken, strengthen, or interrupt the path.
scenes.visual: The connected path glows once, then three small question marks appear at the river, layer boundary, and animals. The Bay remains full-frame and moving.
scenes.narration: A useful model follows the change from its starting point to each connected part. It also asks what could weaken, strengthen, or interrupt the path.

scenes.tts: That makes the model useful for evidence, not just memorizing arrows. Evidence can test each link instead of only the first and last.
scenes.caption: That makes the model useful for evidence, not just memorizing arrows. Evidence can test each link instead of only the first and last.
scenes.visual: A moving highlight tests each connection in order. Check marks remain neutral gold rather than implying proof, and the final question mark stays visible.
scenes.narration: That makes the model useful for evidence, not just memorizing arrows. Evidence can test each link instead of only the first and last.
